content.text:
I found two likely explanations for the hook errors, plus a defect in the commit guard:

- **Codex hooks are awaiting trust review.** `entire doctor` reports eight installed hooks with no approval record. Codex skips changed project hooks until they are reviewed through `/hooks`, as the [official OpenAI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) describes.
- **Claude hooks have configuration drift.** `entire doctor` reports that [`.claude/settings.json`](/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp-plugins/.claude/settings.json) no longer matches what the installed Entire CLI expects, so some Entire events may not fire.
- **The commit guard has a confirmed bypass.** [`is_commit_command()`](/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp-plugins/scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py:14) recognizes `git commit` but misses `rtk git commit`, the form required by this repo’s shell instructions. It also checks only staged schema changes, so `git commit -am ...` can commit an unstaged change to a tracked schema without triggering that check.

The hook unit tests pass, and the generated Codex bundle currently passes `--check`; neither test catches those bypasses. Entire reports Cursor and OpenCode as healthy. The removal of Gemini’s Entire hooks matches this CLI version’s retired Gemini support. I did not change the existing worktree edits.

The immediate user action is to review the Codex hooks with `/hooks`. For Claude, `entire enable --force` is the CLI’s suggested repair, but it would rewrite hook configuration that currently has uncommitted edits; review that diff before applying it.
